title: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Posture Review - Cedarpoint Health
summary: Redwood team reviewed SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 posture with Cedarpoint Health. Discussed evidence, Trust Center access, controls mapping to Cedarpoint control framework, RBAC/SSO requirements, audit logs retention, encryption/KMS and HSM options, and data residency for EU patients. Agreed next steps: share latest reports, grant compliance portal access, and schedule follow-up controls mapping workshop.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment

transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2025-10-08 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Gonzalez (CISO, Cedarpoint), Ethan Ross (Head of Eng), Priya Kumar (Cloud Security), Liam O'Neill (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick posture review focused on SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts, trust center access, and detailed controls mapping next steps.

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate you taking the time today. i'm avery from Redwood, i'll kick us off. samir's here on the sec engineering side.
[00:08] Maya Gonzalez: hi thanks, maya here, CISO at cedarpoint. we wanted to run through your SOC 2 and ISO posture, and make sure we can map controls to our internal framework.
[00:14] Samir Patel: great, thanks maya. quick agenda: we'll surface the reports we can share, show how to get into the trust center / compliance portal, talk about SSO/RBAC, audit logs and retention, and encryption/KMS options, then open to q's.
[00:26] Ethan Ross: sounds good, timeline wise we have Q4 compliance window so we'd like to lock anything needed for vendor sign-off by mid november.
[00:34] Priya Kumar: just to add, we are particularly concerned about data residency for EU patients and key management — we use AWS KMS with an HSM-backed plan for some PII flows.
[00:45] Avery Chen: totally understood. quick note on artifacts: we can provide the SOC 2 Type 2 report, the ISO 27001 cert, plus an evidence bundle summary. full evidence bundles sometimes require an NDA or an SSP access request — we'll walk through that.
[00:58] Liam O'Neill: on procurement, we just need the certs and the right contact for vendor security attestation, and an idea of what controls you map to SOC 2 so we can align internally.
[01:07] Samir Patel: right, and for trust center access we can give you a read-only compliance portal link; it includes our mapping matrix and common artifacts. i'll provision that after the call.
[01:16] Maya Gonzalez: can you confirm whether you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) or HSM integration for private deployments?
[01:23] Samir Patel: yes — for Redwood Private we offer customer-managed KMS and HSM workflows. for hosted API we support envelope encryption with customer KMS via a BYOK flow in most regions — there are some limitations in certain regions due to cloud provider constraints.
[01:37] Ethan Ross: when you say BYOK, is it a true customer key in our KMS or do you hold the key?
[01:42] Samir Patel: the model is envelope encryption: the customer holds the master key in their KMS, we use a short-lived data key for runtime which is rotated. for dedicated/private installs we can configure HSM-based key escrow where you control the root.
[01:54] Maya Gonzalez: ok that helps. another item: audit logs retention — what's the default retention and can we export logs to our SIEM?
[02:00] Avery Chen: default retention in hosted is 90 days for detailed request logs, 365 for aggregated billing traces; we can ship logs to S3 or stream to your SIEM via secure connector. dedicated/private options can be configured for longer retention and direct S3 delivery into your account.
[02:15] Priya Kumar: do the logs include token-level metadata or full prompts? we have PII concerns.
[02:20] Samir Patel: good question. by default we redact PII from logs and we do not persist full user prompts in the long-term logs for hosted customers unless you opt in for debug. for private/dedicated you can choose retention and whether to persist full prompts — many customers use prefix caching and masked logs.
[02:36] Maya Gonzalez: is there an enterprise contract clause for data residency? we have EU patient data that must remain in eu zones.
[02:42] Avery Chen: yes — we support region pinning for both hosted and dedicated. for true EU-only data residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private in an EU region. we can include a data residency addendum in the contract.
[02:55] Ethan Ross: we'd also like to understand your control mappings — do you provide a mapping against common frameworks like ISO 27001 annex and our internal SOC catalog?
[03:04] Samir Patel: we maintain controls mapping in the trust center — SOC 2 to our technical and process controls, and ISO 27001 Annex A mappings. i'll share the mapping matrix. it includes owner, evidence type, and sample artifacts.
[03:16] Maya Gonzalez: sometimes these mapping matrices have gaps — are you open to a joint workshop where we map cedarpoint controls to your artifacts and identify gaps?
[03:23] Avery Chen: absolutely, that’s the plan. we typically run a 60–90 minute controls mapping session with security + engineering and prepare an action log for any gaps.
[03:33] Priya Kumar: about SSO, we use Okta with SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning. we'd need RBAC roles and ability to set per-team rate limits. does redwood support SCIM and fine-grained roles?
[03:44] Samir Patel: yes, Okta SAML + SCIM supported. we have several built-in roles and you can create custom roles with scoped permissions. rate limits are per API key / token and can be configured per org or per team on dedicated deployments.
[03:58] Liam O'Neill: any independence assurance — like independent audits or pen test windows?
[04:03] Avery Chen: we run annual third-party SOC 2 audits and yearly penetration tests with an external firm. the pentest reports are summary-level in the trust center; full reports require an NDA.
[04:12] Maya Gonzalez: can you share last pen test date and high-level findings?
[04:16] Samir Patel: last pentest was June 2025; high-level findings were low/medium issues, most around dependency patching and minor config drift — we've remediated with verified evidence.
[04:27] Ethan Ross: regarding private deployment options, how much effort is typical for an on-prem install? we have some air-gapped locations.
[04:34] Samir Patel: on-prem / air-gap is possible but it's a multi-week project — we provide an appliance-style bundle, install guide, and options for a managed install by Redwood Professional Services. we also support hybrid where control plane is in our VPC but data plane runs in your VPC.
[04:52] Maya Gonzalez: that hybrid model might fit our constraints. question about model artifacts: do you store model weights and are they part of the audit scope?
[04:58] Avery Chen: model weights are part of the runtime artifact; for hosted models we manage weights but logs and prompts are controlled per customer policy. for private deployments the weights are deployed inside your environment. weights themselves are not typically considered customer data but we include model change controls in our audit scope.
[05:12] Priya Kumar: okay, about evidence: can we get an SSP (system security plan) or do you provide an exported controls workbook?
[05:18] Samir Patel: we have an SSP-style document and a downloadable controls workbook (CSV/XLS) in the trust center. i'll attach that.
[05:27] Liam O'Neill: procurement question — pricing for dedicated vs private, are there minimums and SLA terms?
[05:32] Avery Chen: dedicated is usually a reserved capacity contract with monthly minimums; private has a licensing + support fee. we'll share a short pricing sheet after the call and can spin up a pilot for Q4 to validate latency and throughput.
[05:47] Maya Gonzalez: great — i have a couple compliance-specific clarifications: 1) evidence retention windows for audit purposes, 2) how you prove access control and change management.
[05:57] Samir Patel: evidence retention: we can retain audit evidence for up to 3 years on request (for enterprise contracts), standard hosted retention is 12 months for certain artifacts. access control and change mgmt: we record admin actions in the audit log, use role-based approvals, and PRs are linked to change tickets; we can export change history for an SSO/OIDC admin.
[06:20] Ethan Ross: one more technical: what's your approach to key rotation and key compromise recovery?
[06:25] Samir Patel: rotate master keys per your KMS policy; for envelope keys we rotate data keys frequently; if a key compromise occurs we rotate and provide forensic logs. for private installs you can revoke keys and we can rebuild the node with new keys.
[06:39] Maya Gonzalez: are there any live incidents in the past 12 months we should be aware of?
[06:44] Avery Chen: no major incidents; only a handful of low-severity config incidents with limited exposure, all remediated and captured in postmortems which we can share redacted.
[06:55] Priya Kumar: about certification validity — ISO cert expiry date?
[06:58] Samir Patel: our current ISO 27001 cert is valid through March 2026.
[07:03] Liam O'Neill: procurement again, are there contract terms for subprocessor lists and data flow maps?
[07:09] Avery Chen: yes we publish a subprocessor list in the trust center and a data flow diagram; we can provide an updated map as part of the contract.
[07:20] Ethan Ross: do you offer a SOC 2 bridge letter for customers who need a short-term assurance?
[07:25] Avery Chen: we can issue a bridge letter; typical process is to provide recent audit artifacts and an attestation.
[07:31] Maya Gonzalez: curious about alerting and monitoring — do you expose security metrics to customers or is it internal?
[07:36] Samir Patel: both — for dedicated/private we expose more telemetry; for hosted we provide dashboards in the console and can stream selected metrics to your monitoring stack.
[07:47] Priya Kumar: we require a minimum 90-day log retention for certain regulated flows; you said hosted default is 90 days — would you include a contractual clause for that?
[07:55] Avery Chen: yes that's doable in the enterprise contract for the scoped flows.
[08:00] Ethan Ross: ok, let's talk practical next steps — we want the SOC 2 Type 2 report, iso cert, the mapping workbook, and trust center access. can you also run a short bench to show latency/throughput for our typical seq lengths?
[08:12] Samir Patel: sure — for benching we typically run a small POC in a dedicated pool using your sample prompts and sequences. that will take a week to spin up once we get the expected qps and sample payload.
[08:24] Maya Gonzalez: one more question — do you provide any guarantees around model output retention? for compliance we need to show that certain outputs aren't stored.
[08:31] Samir Patel: by default we don't persist full outputs unless explicitly enabled. we can provide a policy and contractual language that we don't store outputs for specified endpoints.
[08:40] Liam O'Neill: good. anything else on your side?
[08:44] Avery Chen: i think that's most of it, we'll follow up with artifacts. we'll also include an invite for the controls mapping workshop.
[08:51] Maya Gonzalez: thanks — we'll review artifacts and get Priya to coordinate the mapping workshop timing.
[08:56] Ethan Ross: ok thanks team.
[09:00] -- end of recording --

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors and run-on lines. references to product names: "Redwood Dedicated" and "Redwood Private" mentioned; trust center = Redwood compliance portal. Some words like "k v cash" or "k v cache" may appear in raw transcript (speaker says KV cache).
notes: Provisioned trust center access, shared next step deadlines. Customer requested SOC 2 Type 2, ISO cert, mapping workbook, and a controls workshop. Procurement needs pricing and data residency addendum.
